## In brief - ECB and SNB left interest rates unchanged. - The interest rate differential affects the CHF/EUR exchange rate. - The SNB is ready to intervene in the foreign exchange market.
## Key Facts - **What**: ECB and SNB left interest rates unchanged. - When: ECB on 23 July, SNB on 18 June. - Where: Decisions taken in Frankfurt and Zurich. - Who: ECB and SNB. - Amount: ECB rates: 2.25%, 2.40%, 2.65%. SNB rate: 0%.
At six in the morning, at the customs of Chiasso or Ponte Chiasso, the queue of cars is already long. Those who travel it every day to go to work have learned to check the exchange rate of the day even before traffic: it is now an automatic gesture, because the salary arrives in francs and the groceries, rent, mortgage remain in euros. On July 23, the European Central Bank left its key interest rates unchanged, confirming the pause after the June hike. The Swiss National Bank, for its part, had already been stuck at zero since June 18.
For those who live on this double border, the simultaneous shutdown of the two central banks is not a detail for a news agency: it defines the terrain on which the exchange rate will move in the coming weeks.
The Governing Council of the ECB confirmed the three key rates at the same levels as those set with the hike on 11 June: the deposit rate at 2.25%, the rate on the main refinancing operations at 2.40%, the rate on marginal loans at 2.65%, all of which have been in force since 17 June. The reason for the pause is uncertainty over energy prices — which have risen, the central bank explains, well above pre-conflict levels in the Middle East, whose impact on inflation has not yet fully manifested itself. There are no commitments made in advance: the approach remains meeting by meeting, with the stated aim of stabilising inflation at 2% over the medium term. The next appointment is on 9-10 September, when the Governing Council will travel to Berlin at the invitation of the Deutsche Bundesbank.
The SNB had anticipated the move by a good month. On June 18, it left its policy rate unchanged at 0%, with Swiss inflation forecast at 0.6% for 2026 and 2027 and 0.7% for 2028 — levels that Zurich considers consistent with its price stability mandate. In the same statement, the central bank said something that weighs more than the key interest rate figure: a greater willingness to intervene in the foreign exchange market to contain an excessive appreciation of the franc, fueled by the uncertain geopolitical climate. This is where the two decisions talk to each other. A wider rate differential tends to make the franc relatively more attractive to those seeking a haven from volatility, supporting its value against the euro. An SNB that is ready to intervene is pushing in the opposite direction, to contain precisely that strengthening. Which of the two forces will prevail is not decided at the table: it depends on how inflation, energy prices and capital flows evolve in the coming weeks, not on a statement published today. It is worth saying clearly: this article describes monetary policy decisions that have already been made public, not exchange rate forecasts or investment advice. For significant amounts, the reference remains a qualified consultant.
Between the end of summer and mid-September, two events focus attention. The first is the ECB meeting on 9-10 September in Berlin: the central bank has hinted that a new hike remains possible if the energy shock worsens. The second is the SNB's quarterly valuation, which is expected around the same time — some market calendars indicate the end of September, but at the time of writing, the SNB had not yet published an official date. However, it has already shown with its announcement in June that it considers the level of the franc a priority.
What to do, then, before those two dates:
- Mark 9-10 September (ECB decision) and the SNB quarterly assessment expected in the same period: these are the times when the picture can change. - If you have a scheduled conversion — salary, transfer, mortgage — check the SNB reference exchange rate of the same day, not the one from a week before. - Don't rely on a single statement from the ECB or the SNB to decide the timing of a transaction: both follow a meeting-by-meeting approach and can change emphasis quickly. - Read the official statement, not just the title of a summary article: the language of reservations — "depends on the data" — is often the most informative part.
Central banks are moving at different speeds, and no one can tell you for sure where the exchange rate will be in September. What you can check today is how many euros you really receive for your francs. ## In brief • Switzerland is preparing for a possible financial earthquake. • The reform of the management of unemployment benefits for cross-border commuters could cost the Confederation one billion. • The new law provides for Switzerland to pay unemployment benefits to cross-border commuters.
• **What**: The reform of the management of unemployment benefits for cross-border workers. • When: April 2026. • Where: Switzerland. • Who: Cross-border commuters. • Amount: CHF 1 billion.
Switzerland is preparing for a possible financial earthquake. After more than ten years of complex negotiations in Brussels, the European Union has given the green light to a reform that could upset the Confederation's accounts. At the center of the debate is the management of unemployment benefits for cross-border workers, a change that closely affects the pockets of Bern and the lives of thousands of Italian, French and German workers.
With the new principle of Lex Locis Laboris, the music changes: the benefit will have to be paid by the country in which the contributions were paid. In simple terms, if a worker living in Italy loses his job in a Ticino company, Switzerland will have to pay for his unemployment.
The weight of the measure is closely linked to volumes. At the end of 2025, the number of active cross-border commuters in Switzerland reached 410,000, an absolute record in Europe. According to rumors collected by the Aargauer Zeitung relaunched by the Corriere del Ticino, the economic impact for the Swiss coffers would be enormous:
Minimum estimate: 500 million francs per year. Maximum estimate: almost 1 billion francs per year.
These figures vary according to the economic situation, but which nevertheless represent an unprecedented burden on the Swiss social system.
The French "hole": the frightening example
To understand the extent of the problem, just look at what happened in France. Between 2011 and 2023, the French unemployment fund (Unedic) accumulated a deficit of 9 billion euros precisely because of the current rules on cross-border commuters. In 2024 alone, the negative balance was 860 million.
The EU reform aims to remedy these distortions, but shifts the economic burden directly onto Switzerland's shoulders.
Bern's resistance and the political knot
Switzerland has not stood idly by. Together with Luxembourg, Bern has long tried to put the brakes on the reform, raising doubts about its ability to control beneficiaries residing abroad. While Luxembourg could obtain a transition period of up to seven years, for the Confederation the game remains open and very delicate.
In addition to the economic aspect, there is the political aspect. The dossier risks becoming fuel on the fire in the debate on relations between Switzerland and the EU and on free movement, fueling the campaigns of critics of bilateral agreements (such as the one linked to the "10 million" initiative).

The Lombardy Region aims to increase salaries of doctors and nurses working in public structures within a radius of twenty kilometers from the Swiss border by 20%. The measure aims to make Italian border hospitals attractive, where professionals are increasingly difficult to engage due to salaries across the border that are three or four times higher than those in Italy. ### How much does the contribution collect from frontiersmen Translated into concrete figures, the provision translates into a retributive increase of around ten thousand euros per year for each doctor and 5,400 euros per year for each nurse in service in the border area. The financing of this measure, not burdening central coffers, is guaranteed by a contribution requested from workers residing in Italy employed in Switzerland under the discipline of old frontiersmen. For a worker earning the equivalent of four thousand Swiss francs net per month, the rate involves a deduction of around 120 euros per month in favour of the National Health Service. The provision is defended by Regional Councillor Massimo Sertori, who reiterates the goodness of the regional choice of applying the contribution starting from the minimum percentage of 3%, even in the presence of a state law that allows going up to 6% of net income. Those who have held the G permit since before July 2023 fall under the transitional regime and benefit from the historical mechanism of exclusive cross-border taxation. For 27 years the old frontier workers have benefited from the benefits of the Italian National Health Service together with their family members, while paying the tax at source exclusively to the Swiss authorities and without having to pay income taxes to the Italian Revenue Agency.
Until 1999, commuters paid sick pay in Switzerland for their own personal coverage and paid a bill of about 600 thousand lire to guarantee assistance to their family members in Italy. With the transition of health management to the Regions and the introduction of the agreement between Switzerland and the European Union on the right of option, the framework has changed. Each border worker had the right to choose within three months of hiring whether to subscribe to the Swiss LAMal coverage (with premiums starting from about 350 euros per month for the individual worker) or rely on the Italian SSN. item.title: Frontier workers: it matters where you work, not the company headquarters
item.description: The Revenue Agency clarifies: the tax regime of frontier workers depends on the place of the physical service, not on the employer's address.
item.content:encoded:
## In a nutshell - The employer's registered office may be outside the border area - Counts the physical place where the work is performed - Basic requirement: residence within 20 km of the border - The limits for teleworking set at 25% per year have been confirmed
## Key facts - **What**: Answer question no. 126/2026 Revenue Agency - When: Enforcement of post-Agreement 2020 legislation - Where: Border area (Lombardy, Piedmont, Ticino, Graubünden) - Who: Scientific informant resident in Ticino - Amount: Deductible of 10,000 euros for new frontier workers
The Revenue Agency has dissolved an interpretative knot that burdened thousands of cross-border workers through the answer to call no. 126/2026. The case under consideration concerns a worker residing in a Swiss border municipality in the Canton of Ticino, employed as a scientific informant of the drug. The professional operates entirely in Lombardy, therefore within 20 km of the Swiss border, but on behalf of a company that has its registered office in Veneto, a region totally unrelated to the map of border areas. The central question was whether the geographical location of the employer's administrative headquarters could preclude access to the preferential tax regime provided for by the New Agreement between Italy and Switzerland.
### The primacy of physical performance
The Tax Office has determined that the tax status of the worker is governed by ## Old and new border crossers: the differences in the withdrawal
The Revenue Agency's clarification fits into a tax system now divided into two distinct tracks. The so-called old frontier workers are those who worked in Switzerland for at least one day between 31 December 2018 and 17 July 2023. For this category, the agreement guarantees the maintenance of the exclusive taxation regime at source in Switzerland, with a total IRPEF exemption in Italy. This right remains valid even in the event of a change of employer, provided that the interruption of the relationship does not exceed 12 months and that the new employment remains in the border area.
### The New Hire Mechanism
For those who started the business from 18 July 2023, the situation changes radically towards a competing taxation model. In this scenario, Switzerland applies a reduced source tax, equal to 80% of the ordinary tax calculated according to the cantonal tables. The worker is then required to present the [dichiarazione dei redditi](nav:tax-return) in Italy. Here, the entire income is subject to IRPEF taxation, but with specific mitigation mechanisms: an exemption deductible of 10,000 euros and the full deductibility of Swiss mandatory social security contributions, such as [AVS](nav:pension) and [LPP](nav:pension). To avoid double taxation, a tax credit is recognized for what has already been paid to the Swiss authorities.
A critical aspect concerns the management of the smart ## Procedures and checks for the worker
To benefit correctly from the tax regime, the worker must ensure that their contractual and logistical situation complies with the parameters defined by interpello 126/2026. The first step is to verify the kilometric distance between the municipality of residence and the border, which must be less than or equal to 20 km. Subsequently, it is necessary for the employment contract or a statement from the employer to clearly specify that the performance takes place within the border area, regardless of where the company's legal headquarters is located. This document is essential in case of checks by Italian tax authorities.
### Declaration obligations and deadlines
New border workers must pay particular attention to the completion of specific tables in the Redditi or 730 model. It is necessary to report the Swiss gross income, deduct pension contributions and apply the €10,000 exemption. The calculation of the tax credit requires proof of payments made in Switzerland for income tax at source. Even old border workers, although enjoying exemption, must monitor any changes in their situation, such as exceeding the 12-month inactivity limit that could make them lose the transitional regime of favor.
The tax authority's decision represents a revolution for Italian companies located far from the border that intend to take advantage of professionals residing in Switzerland. The possibility of correctly classifying these workers as border workers, even with headquarters in Venice or Rome, opens up new recruitment opportunities without creating tax uncertainty for the employee. To calculate with precision the impact of taxes on the payroll and check the actual net, it is possible to use the dedicated [calculator](nav:calculator), which takes into account the current tax rates and the allowances provided for by law 83/2023.
It is recommended to always keep copies of residence certificates and time sheets that attest to physical presence in the border area, especially for itinerant professions such as scientific informants. Compliance with the requirements for daily commuting remains an indispensable pillar for maintaining access to the tax benefits provided by the Italian-Swiss order.

Porto Ceresio, overlooking Lake Lugano a few kilometres from the Ponte Tresa crossing and from Gaggiolo, is a frequent residential choice for those who obtain a G permit and work in Mendrisiotto or Lugano. The geographical location makes commuting short, but the economic convenience depends entirely on the regulatory framework that regulates border crossers.
### Taxation: where to pay The key rule, confirmed by the Double Taxation Convention signed on 9 December 1976 and reiterated by the New Frontier Agreement, provides that the tax at source on income from employment is withheld only in Switzerland. The time gain translates into lower fuel cost, less car wear and more free hours.

The New Frontier Agreement has modified the calculation basis: from 2024 the refunds are parameterized to the net taxable income of the deductibles (7,500 or 10,000 euros). For the single border crossing there is no direct fulfillment: it is the Municipality that collects and decides how to reinvest (services, kindergartens, transport).

## Key facts - **What**: Transfer of residence for cross-border work - When: From 1 January 2024 (new tax regime) - Where: Maccagno with Pine and Veddasca (VA) - Who: Revenue Agency and AFC/ESTV - Amount: Deductible 10,000 euros for new frontier workers
Maccagno con Pino and Veddasca is one of the most strategic destinations for those who decide to pursue a career as a border worker in Canton Ticino, especially for those who work in the district of Locarno or Bellinzona. Located on the eastern shore of Lake Maggiore, this municipality in the province of Varese offers immediate access to the Zenna pass, drastically reducing travel times compared to other towns more distant from the border. However, the choice to reside in this location involves a series of essential regulatory and tax assessments, dictated by the New Frontier Agreement signed on 23 December 2020 and ratified by Law 83 of 13 June 2023.
### The logistics of commuting from Maccagno From a logistical point of view, the municipality extends over a territory that includes several mountain villages in the Veddasca Valley and lakeside areas such as Pino. For a worker with [permesso G](nav:permits), the proximity to Switzerland is the advantage Fiscal and Social Security Analysis for Cross-Border Workers
The current regulatory framework is defined by the Double Taxation Convention of December 9, 1976, and the recent agreement in force since January 1, 2024. For a cross-border worker residing in Maccagno, the withholding tax on employment income is deducted only in Switzerland. To avoid double taxation, Italy applies the tax credit mechanism through the CE section of Model 730 or Redditi PF. A crucial element is the exemption: new cross-border workers are entitled to a €10,000 exemption, while 'old' cross-border workers (those active before July 17, 2023) have a €7,500 exemption, with a transitional regime covering 2024–2033. This difference directly impacts the calculation of the net paycheck (nav:payslip) and family financial planning.
Swiss Social Contributions and Pension System
Working in Canton Ticino means contributing to the Swiss social security system. The applicable rates are precise: the AVS/AI/IPG contribution is 5.3% paid by the employee, while unemployment insurance (AD/AC) applies at 1.1% up to a ceiling of CHF 148,200. Additional contributions include LAINF (0.7–1.5%) and the second pillar (LPP), with rates ranging from 7% to 18% depending on the worker's age bracket, starting from 25 years old. In Italy, income exceeding the exemption is taxed at the current IRPEF rates: 23% up to €28,000, 35% between €28,001 and €50,000, and 43% over €50,000. Therefore, it is essential to use a [calculator](nav:calculator) to accurately estimate the total tax burden.
Pension Management and Fiscal Residency
Managing pension contributions is a fundamental pillar. Besides AVS and LPP, many workers opt for the third pillar 3a to benefit from tax advantages and to supplement future retirement income. Residing in Maccagno allows maintaining fiscal residence in Italy while operating within the Swiss economic context, but requires careful management of deadlines communicated by the Revenue Agency and the Ministry of Economy and Finance. Transparency between tax administrations, coordinated at the federal level by the AFC/ESTV, ensures that every income is correctly registered and taxed according to bilateral agreements.
## Useful tools for your case To verify your within/over 20 km tax scenario, use the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator) and the [tax return guide](nav:tax-return). Practical Procedures and Health Insurance Transferring to Maccagno involves activating specific procedures to regularize your status. The first step is obtaining the [Permesso G](nav:permits), issued by the Ticino cantonal authorities upon request from the employer. Simultaneously, the issue of health insurance arises. According to LAMal, cross-border workers have the so-called right of option: they can choose to insure themselves in Switzerland or remain within the Italian healthcare system. If choosing LAMal, one must consider the deductibles for adults, which range from CHF 300 to CHF 2,500. This choice must be made within three months from the start of employment or from the transfer of residence, and is often irreversible unless significant changes occur in the employment situation.
Operational Steps for the Transfer For those deciding to settle in Maccagno, the procedure includes: - Registration with the Maccagno with Pino and Veddasca Municipality. - Communicating the new residence to the Swiss employer for updating the work permit. - Evaluating the health insurance option [LAMal](nav:health) within the deadlines set by the UFSP/BAG. - Opening a technical bank account with Swiss banks to receive salary in CHF, carefully evaluating exchange costs using a comparison tool. - Preparing documentation for the annual tax declaration in Italy, including certifications of INPS contributions and taxes paid in Switzerland.
Living in a border municipality like Maccagno also offers advantages related to 'ristorni', the tax shares that Switzerland retrocedes to Italian municipalities to finance public works and local services. Although the new agreement gradually modifies this system, residents continue to benefit from infrastructure maintained thanks to these financial flows. Before signing a rental or purchase contract in Maccagno, it is advisable to perform a comprehensive simulation of the net available income to understand the actual purchasing power, considering that the cost of living in this area is influenced by the proximity to Ticino. For a precise calculation of taxes and net salary, you can consult our [calculator](nav:calculator) dedicated to cross-border workers.

item.title: Cross-border commuters: Ticino applies the full withholding rate
item.description: Opting for the Omnibus Decree now means being taxed in Ticino at 100% of the tables instead of 80%. There is time until the end of 2026 to regularise.
item.content:encoded:
Since January 2026 the Canton of Ticino withholding tax office has been applying the full rate — 100% of tables A, B, C and H — to cross-border commuters who choose the Omnibus Decree mechanism. Until 2025 the same workers were taxed at 80%, as "new cross-border commuters". The communication was made public by OCST, the canton's most representative trade union.
## Who is affected
The measure concerns a specific group, which OCST calls the "old cross-border commuters from the new municipalities". These are workers who:
- worked in Ticino between 31 December 2018 and 17 July 2023, returning home daily; - have their tax residence in an Italian municipality within 20 km of the border; - live in a municipality that was nevertheless absent from the Canton of Ticino's old list of border municipalities.
It is the last point that makes the difference, and it is the one most often misunderstood. Being within 20 km is not enough: anyone resident in a municipality already on the old list is unaffected by this communication.
## A two-part mechanism
The tax burden on these workers arises from the interaction of two rules, one Swiss and one Italian.
In Switzerland they pay withholding tax, deducted by the employer on the basis of tables — A, B, C and H — that vary with family circumstances. Until 2025 Ticino applied 80% of the ordinary rate to this group, the treatment reserved for "new cross-border commuters".
In Italy, the Omnibus Decree allows workers to opt for a substitute tax equal to 25% of the withholding tax already paid in Switzerland. Adding the two together, the overall burden was broadly in line with that of "classic" old cross-border commuters: those who pay no direct income tax in Italy but are subject to the full rate in Switzerland. ## What changes
The withholding tax office has determined that anyone opting for the Omnibus mechanism is to be taxed in Ticino at 100% of the tables, no longer at 80%. The balance described above breaks down: the full Swiss rate applies, and the Italian share is added on top.
Workers face two options, each with a cost.
**First option, the Omnibus route.** Withholding tax at 100% in Switzerland, plus the Italian substitute tax of 25% calculated on the amount paid in Switzerland.
**Second option, staying at 80%.** The Swiss rate remains reduced, but the worker is classified for all purposes as a "new cross-border commuter", with the Italian filing consequences that follow.
One point deserves to be stated plainly: the "100%" here is the full rate set by the tax tables, not 100% of the salary. What changes is the percentage applied, not the entire wage.
### An example with hypothetical figures
The values below serve only to illustrate how the calculation works. The actual rate depends on the applicable table, the municipality and family circumstances, and should be checked against your own salary certificate.
Assume gross annual income of 60,000 francs and a full withholding tax of 6,000 francs, that is 10% of gross pay.
- Under the Omnibus option, 6,000 francs are paid in Switzerland, to which the Italian substitute tax is added, calculated as 0.25 × 6,000 = 1,500 francs. The total is 7,500 francs. - Staying at 80%, 4,800 francs are paid in Switzerland, but the position must then be handled in Italy under the rules applicable to new cross-border commuters.
The difference therefore depends on your effective rate: there is no single answer that fits everyone. For an estimate of your own case, start with the [net salary calculator](nav:calculator). ## What to do now
There is time until the end of 2026 to regularise your position. The first step is working out which category you fall into, and that requires two concrete pieces of information.
1. **Check your municipality of tax residence.** Being within 20 km of the border is not enough: you need to know whether that municipality appeared on the Canton of Ticino's old list of border municipalities. That is the criterion separating those affected from those who are not. 2. **Reconstruct your periods of work in Ticino between 31 December 2018 and 17 July 2023**, with evidence of daily return. Contracts, salary certificates and employer attestations are the documents that count.
That done, the choice between the Omnibus option and the 80% rate must be assessed against the figures on your own payslip, not in the abstract: the outcome changes with the applicable table and family circumstances. A tax adviser who regularly handles cross-border cases is the right person for the simulation. OCST provides assistance to its members.
## The underlying issue is political
The situation stems from an ambiguity that has dragged on for years: two countries reading the same group of workers differently. According to OCST the way out is not individual but political — action by the Italian state with Bern to settle the treatment of these workers once and for all.
Until then the choice rests with the individual worker, against a deadline set for the end of 2026. Anyone in the group described above would be well advised not to wait until the final months: reconstructing work periods and documentation takes time.
The [tax return guide](nav:tax-return) may help in weighing up the two filing regimes.
*Source: [ilgiorno.it](https://www.ilgiorno.it/sondrio/cronaca/caso-frontalieri-altre-tasse-0066da70), 25 January 2026, based on the OCST communication.*
